# Student test results

**On New York's grades 3–8 English Language Arts (ELA) and Mathematics tests, Cambridge's proficiency rates — the share of students scoring at or above grade level — were at or above the middle of the five districts shown here in most years through 2021–22. Since the tests changed in 2022–23, Cambridge's ELA rate has been the lowest or second-lowest of the five.** In 2023–24, about 41% of Cambridge students tested proficient in ELA and 53% in Math, compared with statewide rates of about 46% and 54%.

These results come from New York's **Report Card Database**, which reports test results for every district. The chart below shows how Cambridge's ELA proficiency rate has changed since 2014–15, alongside nearby districts for context.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    geom_line,
    geom_point,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_color_manual,
    scale_x_continuous,
    scale_y_continuous,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc

# Find repo root to locate data (works from Jupyter context)
def _find_repo_root():
    cwd = Path.cwd()
    for base in [cwd, *cwd.parents][:5]:
        if (base / "data" / "crosswalks").is_dir():
            return base
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find repo root")

REPO_ROOT = _find_repo_root()
PROCESSED_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "processed"

# Load assessments panel
assessments = pl.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIR / "assessments_em_ela_math.parquet")

# Last school year (ending) shown on this page. The panel also holds 2025-26
# (year_end 2026), released by NYSED in November 2026; it is held back until the
# chapter is reworked. Raising this number requires rereading every sentence
# below: the checks at the end of this cell fail if the prose no longer matches.
LAST_YEAR_SHOWN = 2025
assessments = assessments.filter(pl.col("year_end") <= LAST_YEAR_SHOWN)


def year_label(year_end: int) -> str:
    """2024 -> '2023–24'."""
    return f"{year_end - 1}–{str(year_end)[2:]}"


# Helper: proficiency rate for group (All Students, grades 3-8 aggregate)
def proficiency_for(group: dict[str, str], subject: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Proficiency rate (pct_prof) for All Students, grades 3-8, by district-year."""
    region_by_cd = {
        cd: ("Washington County" if cd in cc.WASHINGTON_K12 else "Other comparison districts")
        for cd in group
    }
    return (
        assessments.filter(
            pl.col("nysed_district_cd").is_in(list(group))
            & (pl.col("subgroup") == "All Students")
            & (pl.col("grade") == "3-8")
            & (pl.col("subject") == subject)
            # NYSED does not publish the grades 3-8 total for every district-year
            & pl.col("pct_prof").is_not_null()
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("nysed_district_cd").replace_strict(group).alias("district"),
            pl.col("nysed_district_cd").replace_strict(region_by_cd).alias("region"),
        )
        .select("district", "region", "year_end", "pct_prof")
        .sort("district", "year_end")
    )


def statewide(subject: str, year_end: int) -> float:
    return assessments.filter(
        (pl.col("entity_level") == "state")
        & (pl.col("subgroup") == "All Students")
        & (pl.col("grade") == "3-8")
        & (pl.col("subject") == subject)
        & (pl.col("year_end") == year_end)
    )["pct_prof"].item()


# --- Checks: the numbers written out in the prose must match the data. --------
def _rate(subject: str, district: str, year_end: int) -> float:
    g = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, subject)
    return g.filter(
        (pl.col("district") == district) & (pl.col("year_end") == year_end)
    )["pct_prof"].item()


def _rank(subject: str, year_end: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(Cambridge's rank from the top, number of districts with a rate)."""
    g = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, subject).filter(pl.col("year_end") == year_end)
    mine = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)["pct_prof"].item()
    return int((g["pct_prof"] > mine).sum()) + 1, g.height


_years = sorted(proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, "ELA")["year_end"].unique())
assert (_years[0], _years[-1]) == (2015, 2025), _years
assert 2020 not in _years
assert round(_rate("ELA", cc.FOCUS, 2024), 1) == 41.1
assert round(_rate("Math", cc.FOCUS, 2024), 1) == 53.2
assert round(statewide("ELA", 2024), 1) == 46.3
assert round(statewide("Math", 2024), 1) == 54.3
# ELA: at or above the middle (rank <= 3 of 5) through 2021-22 ...
assert all(_rank("ELA", y)[0] <= 3 for y in _years if y <= 2022)
# ... and lowest or second-lowest of five since 2022-23.
assert all(_rank("ELA", y) in [(4, 5), (5, 5)] for y in _years if y >= 2023)
# 2023-24: ELA lowest of five; Math fourth of five; Schuylerville highest in both.
assert _rank("ELA", 2024) == (5, 5) and _rank("Math", 2024) == (4, 5)
for _s in ("ELA", "Math"):
    _g = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, _s).filter(pl.col("year_end") == 2024)
    assert _g.sort("pct_prof", descending=True)["district"][0] == "Schuylerville"
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ela-proficiency
#| fig-cap: "Percent of students at/above proficiency on grades 3–8 ELA tests, by school year ending, 2015 (2014–15) through 2025 (2024–25). Tests were cancelled in 2020; in 2021 about half as many students statewide took the tests as in 2019. Results are comparable within three eras (see text). Source: NYSED Report Card Database."
g = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, "ELA")
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "pct_prof", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=sorted(g["year_end"].unique()))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Percent proficient",
        title=(
            f"Grades 3–8 ELA proficiency, "
            f"{year_label(g['year_end'].min())} to {year_label(g['year_end'].max())}"
        ),
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

Cambridge's ELA proficiency rate has fluctuated, as have all districts'. The 2020–21 rates are not representative. Tests were cancelled entirely in spring 2020, and in spring 2021 only about half as many students statewide took them as in 2019. Several districts' rates that year are unusually high.

The Math proficiency picture is similar:

```{python}
#| label: fig-math-proficiency
#| fig-cap: "Percent of students at/above proficiency on grades 3–8 Math tests, by school year ending, 2015 (2014–15) through 2025 (2024–25). A missing point means NYSED did not publish a grades 3–8 Math total for that district in that year. Source: NYSED Report Card Database."
g = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, "Math")
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "pct_prof", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=sorted(g["year_end"].unique()))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Percent proficient",
        title=(
            f"Grades 3–8 Math proficiency, "
            f"{year_label(g['year_end'].min())} to {year_label(g['year_end'].max())}"
        ),
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

The Math chart has gaps: from 2017–18 through 2024–25, NYSED did not publish a grades 3–8 Math total for some districts in some years, including Cambridge in 2021–22. Where both rates are published, Cambridge has been below Schuylerville in every year since 2015–16. It has been above Greenwich and Salem in some years and below them in others.

## Why scores don't compare across all years

New York has **redesigned the tests and changed the passing standards twice** in this 10-year window. As a result, proficiency rates are comparable *within* three eras, but not *across* them:

- **2015–2017 (Common Core era):** Tests under the Common Core standards
- **2018–2022 (Redesign):** New tests and new passing standards adopted in 2018
- **2023–2025 (Next Generation):** New tests aligned to the Next Generation Learning Standards

A change in the proficiency rate *across* one of these boundaries reflects the new standard as much as any change in student learning. For example, the 2017→2018 jump for many districts is largely due to the redesign, not a sudden improvement in student skills.

**2020–21 is an outlier:** Tests were cancelled in spring 2020. In 2021, only about half as many students statewide took the tests as in 2019, so the 2021 rates are not representative and should be read with caution.

## How Cambridge compares: 2023–24

The table below shows where each district stood in 2023–24, the second year of the Next Generation tests. It is the most recent year shown on this page for which NYSED published both rates for all five districts. Results for 2025–26, which NYSED released in November 2026, are not yet included on this page.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-proficiency-2024
#| tbl-cap: "Percent of students at/above proficiency on grades 3–8 ELA and Math tests in 2023–24, by district."
g_ela = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, "ELA").filter(pl.col("year_end") == 2024)
g_math = proficiency_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP, "Math").filter(pl.col("year_end") == 2024)

wide = (
    g_ela.select("district", "region", pct_prof_ela="pct_prof")
    .join(
        g_math.select("district", "region", pct_prof_math="pct_prof"),
        on=["district", "region"],
        how="full",
        coalesce=True,
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("region") == "Washington County").then(0).otherwise(1).alias("_rank")
    )
    .sort(["_rank", "district"])
    .drop("_rank")
)

(
    GT(wide, rowname_col="district", groupname_col="region")
    .tab_header(
        title="Grades 3–8 proficiency, 2023–24",
        subtitle="Percent of students at/above proficiency (All Students)"
    )
    # values are already in percent (41.1 means 41.1%), so do not rescale
    .fmt_number(columns=["pct_prof_ela", "pct_prof_math"], decimals=1, pattern="{x}%")
    .tab_spanner(label="Percent proficient", columns=["pct_prof_ela", "pct_prof_math"])
    .cols_label(pct_prof_ela="ELA", pct_prof_math="Math")
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=[
            loc.body(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
            loc.stub(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
        ],
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** NYSED Report Card Database. School year 2023–24 "
            "(tests given in spring 2024), the second year of the Next "
            "Generation tests."
        )
    )
)
```

In 2023–24, Cambridge's ELA proficiency rate (41.1%) was the lowest of the five districts, and its Math rate (53.2%) was fourth, above Hoosick Falls. Schuylerville had the highest rate in both subjects.
